newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy early retirement needs review - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy early retirement needs review - Prodi.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said on Wednesday that controversial early retirement pensions needed to be re-examined and that total pensions spending should not rise by more than Gross Domestic Product.

"In the period 1997-2000...in the absence of corrective measures, pensions spending will grow around 1.5 percentage points a year more than the forecast rise in real terms of GDP," Prodi said in a document given to union leaders, the employers body Confindustria and trade bodies.
Prodi presented the document at negotiations on reform of the welfare state that opened on Wednesday and are expected to last all summer.
He said official government estimates forecast that the ratio of pension spending to GDP in 1997-2000 would be about 0.5 percentage point higher than the average 1996-97 level.
Prodi said that early retirment schemes, which allow Italians to draw a pension based on length of service rather than because they have reached retirement age, needed review.
"We have to see whether the country can afford to keep... a calculation method that guarantees pension payments independently of what has been contributed," Prodi said.
"That means we must look again at whether the terms for early retirement and/or the way they are calculated are appropriate," he said.
